analysis.gate: Accepted measured-analysis alternative, not a 5x end-to-end claim.
analysis.load_bearing_assumption: Bridge and cycle overhead must dominate for these changes to materially accelerate the whole directionality stage; Colville profiling breaks that assumption for cycle repair.
analysis.colville: Baseline 748.083 ms median, initial refactor 707.997 ms, final rebased tree 714.518 ms (five timed rounds each). Different runs are not statistical proof of the small whole-stage gain.
analysis.attribution: Colville makes zero fix_cycles calls; baseline profiled known-flow assignment 0.551 s and synthetic DEM 0.270 s out of 1.068 s dominate. Bridges drop from 15.406 to 9.961 ms in 20-round direct wall measurements.
analysis.synthetic: 10-edge synthetic fix_cycles median 126.996 ms legacy, 0.535 ms reformulated Python, 0.356 ms Rust; 20 rounds after warmup, deepcopy excluded. This is a cycle-heavy synthetic gain, not a Colville-stage gain.
analysis.native_justification: Final paired core medians: repairable Python 160.866 us vs native 6.929 us; no-terminal exhaustive Python 10.880 ms vs native 61.264 us. One native call per search.
analysis.bounds: Worst case remains exponential, capped at ten flippable edges as before; cap is now checked before subset allocation. Exact minimum-cardinality/input-order choice is retained. Most easy-case savings come from early exit, not Rust.

Neither directionality.py nor delta_directionality.py changed. Rebase was conflict-free, extension rebuilt, both suites rerun.
